title: Collection of Skin Biopsies from Cattle
author: Froylan Sosa
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bm3yk8pw
materials: Restrain the animal in a head chute.
Wipe area with a sterile dry gauze.
Spray tick spray around the biopsy site.

steps.title: Label cassettes
steps.instruction: Label each cassette using a permanent marker (or a pencil) for histology identification.

steps.title: Prepare biopsy site
steps.instruction: Clip the intended biopsy area (typically the middle of the 5th or 6th rib on the thorax, or the shoulder) with clippers, then wipe the area with ethanol‑soaked gauze.

steps.title: Apply local anesthetic
steps.instruction: Spray 5 % lidocaine onto the prepared biopsy area and wait 30 seconds before proceeding.

steps.title: Obtain skin sample
steps.instruction: Using a 5 mm skin punch, rotate the punch while applying mild downward force to excise a skin core.

steps.title: Clean skin punch
steps.instruction: Immerse the skin punch in 70 % ethanol to clean it; the punch may be reused three to four times.

steps.title: Transfer sample to cassette
steps.instruction: Remove the skin core from the punch with a needle or tweezers, place it between the sponges inside a cassette, and close the cassette securely.

steps.title: Fix sample in NBF
steps.instruction: Place the closed cassette into a container containing 10 % neutral buffered formalin (NBF) and keep at room temperature.

steps.title: Apply wound care
steps.instruction: Place sterile gauze on the biopsy site to absorb excess blood, then apply a small amount of super glue to the wound and wait 10 seconds.

steps.title: Post‑fix processing
steps.instruction: Leave the skin samples in NBF for 16–20 hours at room temperature; thereafter rinse the cassettes in PBS twice for 15 minutes each, cut each skin sample in half (using gloves), and store the cassettes in a container filled with PBS.

substeps.instruction: Fix 16–20 h at room temperature in 10 % NBF.
Rinse cassettes in PBS twice, 15 min per rinse.
Cut each skin sample in half while wearing gloves.
